subject: Hospitality
title: AV and Production: Invisible Infrastructure
description: A micro-lesson that makes AV and Production: Invisible Infrastructure usable.

hook.text: AV and Production: a surprising example shows why better reasoning matters.

buildup.text: Hotel AV departments or contracted vendors provide projectors, screens, microphones, mixing boards, staging.

discovery.text: In-house hotel AV carries 50–100% markups over outside vendors. Planners negotiate hard on AV because margins are enormous.

twist.text: Bad AV ruins a keynote faster than a bad speaker. A mic that cuts out or a screen that flickers destroys audience trust instantly.

climax.text: LED walls are replacing projectors for premium events—brighter, seamless, and more impressive.

punchline.text: 20–30% of the budget, 100% of the impact. AV is invisible when perfect.

quiz.question: Why do event planners negotiate hard on hotel AV costs?
options: In-house hotel AV carries 50–100% markups over external vendors
